title: Wisdom in Relationships
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Wisdom in relationships means loving others with discernment, holiness, truth, patience, and good judgment. Biblical love is not naïve; it is shaped by God’s Word and guided by the fear of the Lord.
summary: Wisdom in relationships means loving others with discernment, holiness, truth, patience, and good judgment. Biblical love is not naïve; it is shaped by God’s Word and guided by the fear of the Lord.
christFocus: Jesus Christ loved perfectly with both compassion and discernment. He welcomed sinners, exposed hypocrisy, set boundaries, spoke truth, and always acted according to the Father’s will.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Relationships shape people. Scripture warns that companions influence wisdom, character, and conduct. Believers must be thoughtful about the voices and relationships that form them.

Wisdom does not mean suspicion toward everyone. It means love governed by truth. Some relationships require patience and closeness; others require boundaries, correction, or distance.

God’s wisdom is pure, peaceable, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy, and sincere. This kind of wisdom resists both harshness and foolish compromise.

In Christ, believers are called to put on compassion, humility, forgiveness, love, and peace. Wise relationships are therefore both discerning and gracious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people confuse love with unlimited access, or discernment with coldness. Scripture teaches a better balance: love deeply, but do not abandon wisdom.

This doctrine is especially important for people recovering from manipulation, abuse, addiction patterns, or unhealthy dependency. God does not call His people to foolishness in the name of love.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask God for wisdom in your relationships. Love people sincerely, but test influences, set wise boundaries where needed, and let Scripture shape your decisions. Do not confuse guilt, fear, attraction, or pressure with the leading of the Lord.
